posts.title: Ducks on the edge sleep with one eye open. In a 1999 study, mallards at the end of a sleeping row kept the outward eye open, and the brain half linked to it stayed awake. Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides. #animalfacts #birds #ducks #sleepscience

A village kept falling asleep. From 2013, people in Kalachi, Kazakhstan, fell asleep suddenly, some for days. In 2015 officials blamed gases from a nearby old uranium mine, though the cause is disputed. Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides. #truestory #mystery #kazakhstan #sleepscience

Sleep talking: what do people say in their sleep? In one Paris sleep lab, 232 adults (mostly patients) were recorded: the top word was 'no', and about 1 in 10 clauses had swearing. #sleeptalking #sleep #funnyfacts #sleepscience #didyouknow

Ducks on the edge sleep with one eye open. In a 1999 study, mallards at the end of a sleeping row kept the outward eye open, and the brain half linked to it stayed awake. Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides. #animalfacts #birds #ducks #sleepscience

This seal sleeps while sinking. Brain recordings of wild northern elephant seals showed short naps deep in their dives, drifting down in a spiral: about 2 hours of sleep a day at sea, about 10 on land. Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides. #animalfacts #seals #ocean #sleepscience

Freddy Krueger was inspired by a true story. In the early 1980s, US officials recorded unexplained deaths in sleep among young refugee men, mostly Hmong. Wes Craven said news of them inspired the film. Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides. #truestory #mystery #history #sleepscience

An epidemic left people frozen for decades. Encephalitis lethargica, the "sleeping sickness" of the 1910s and 1920s, left some survivors frozen for decades. In 1969 Oliver Sacks woke some with L-dopa. Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides. #truestory #history #medicalhistory #sleepscience

Why do we dream? What science knows so far. No settled answer: one review links dreams to mind wandering, threat rehearsal has mixed support, and a back-of-brain hot zone tracks dreaming in REM and non-REM sleep. #whydowedream #dreams #dreamscience #psychology #brain

These birds sleep while flying. Brain recordings of wild great frigatebirds showed sleep in flight, in short bouts, about 42 minutes a day, often with one half of the brain awake. Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides. #animalfacts #birds #sleepscience #nature

Two months in a cave. He thought one. In 1962 Michel Siffre lived alone in a cave with no clock and no daylight. When his team came for him on September 14, he thought it was August 20. Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides. #truestory #chronobiology #sleepscience #experiment

Dream about being late for an exam: what science says. 67% of students in one survey had dreamed about school. In France, about 700 medical students' exam dreams mostly went wrong, yet dreaming of the exam went with slightly better grades. #dreammeaning #examdream #dreams #students #sleepscience

Clocks go back on Sunday Oct 25: do you get an extra hour of sleep? In Central Europe 3:00 becomes 2:00 (UK 2:00 to 1:00; US and Canada Nov 1). A 2013 review found little sign of extra sleep, and earlier wake-ups for about five days. #clocksgoback #daylightsaving #sleep #bodyclock #extrahour
A smell changes dreams: scent or mood? In fifteen volunteers, odors during REM shifted the emotional tone of reported dreams. Schredl et al. · 2009. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Sleepwalking: how common is it? A review of 51 studies estimated 6.9% of people have sleepwalked at least once; in a year, about 5% of children and 1.5% of adults. It usually starts in deep non-REM sleep, not REM. #sleepwalking #sleep #parasomnia #sleepscience #didyouknow

Can't sleep before a full moon? One study says it's not just you. In a 2021 field study, sleep was shortest 3 to 5 days before a full moon, varying by 46 to 58 minutes across the cycle. Other studies are mixed. Next full moon: Mon Oct 26. #fullmoon #cantsleep #moon #sleepscience #sleep

Sleeping songbird: silent brain or replay? Some neurons in sleeping adult zebra finches replayed activity patterns linked to daytime singing. Dave & Margoliash · 2000. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Exploding head syndrome: the loud bang as you fall asleep. A sudden noise in your head as you drift off or wake. Usually painless; 18% of 211 US college students said they had had it. If it is frequent or worrying, talk to a doctor. #explodingheadsyndrome #sleep #weirdfacts #sleepscience #brain
Isolated flies: more sleep or less? Chronic social isolation reduced sleep in the studied fruit flies. Li et al. · 2021. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Do you dream in color? Most people under 25 do. In one diary study of 60 people, only 4.4% of under-25s' dreams were black and white, vs about a quarter for over-55s raised on black-and-white media. A link, not proof. #dreams #dreamincolor #dreamscience #sleep #didyouknow
Resting spider: fixed or moving retinas? Resting jumping spiderlings showed bouts of retinal movement, with twitches and leg curls. Rössler et al. · 2022. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Every culture has a name for this demon. Old Hag in Newfoundland, kanashibari in Japan, a ghost pressing on the bed in China: all names for sleep paralysis. What is it called where you live? #sleepparalysis #folklore #truestory #culture

Do blind people dream? Yes. In a 4-week diary study, people blind from birth reported fewer pictures and more sound, touch, taste and smell, and about 25% of their reported dreams were nightmares (6% for sighted people). #blind #dreams #dreamscience #senses #didyouknow
Dolphin vigilance: hours or fifteen days? One tested dolphin maintained near-perfect target detection across a fifteen-day session. Branstetter et al. · 2012. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

"Nightmare" comes from a demon on your chest. In Old English a mare was a spirit thought to sit on sleepers' chests. The word first meant that suffocating feeling, now known from sleep paralysis. #etymology #nightmare #sleepparalysis #didyouknow
Two wild elephants: two or eight hours? Two wild African elephant matriarchs averaged about two hours of daily estimated sleep. Gravett et al. · 2017. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Every night, your brain paralyses you. In REM sleep the brainstem switches off most voluntary muscles so you do not act out your dreams; eye and breathing muscles keep working. #remsleep #sleepscience #dreams #brain

Recurring dreams meaning: what science says. In a 2006 study of 212 recurrent dreams, about two thirds contained a threat, but under 2% fit every prediction of threat rehearsal theory. A hypothesis tested, not settled. #recurringdreams #dreammeaning #dreams #nightmares #psychology
Tired bees: clearer or fuzzier directions? Sleep-deprived honeybees gave less precise direction signals in their waggle dances. Klein et al. · 2010. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Without sleep, every rat died. In Allan Rechtschaffen's experiments at the University of Chicago, all rats kept from sleeping without a break died, usually within 2 to 3 weeks (Sleep, 1989). #sleepscience #science #didyouknow #sleep

After 17 hours awake, you test like you drank. In a 2000 study, 17 to 19 hours without sleep left people as impaired as a 0.05% blood alcohol level on some tests (Williamson & Feyer). #sleepdeprivation #sleepscience #didyouknow #brain

Sleep paralysis: why you can't move when you wake up. In REM sleep your muscles are switched off, and sometimes the mind wakes first. About 8% of people have had it. Scary but short; if it's frequent or worrying, talk to a doctor. #sleepparalysis #sleep #remsleep #scary #sleepscience
Reindeer chewing cud: awake only? Brain recordings suggest reindeer can sleep during rumination. Furrer et al. · 2024. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

A tanker, a reef, and too little sleep. The NTSB found the Exxon Valdez ran aground in 1989 partly because the third mate was fatigued and overworked; it also cited the captain's alcohol impairment and a crew that was not rested. #truestory #exxonvaldez #sleepdeprivation #history

Why can't I remember my dreams? What sleep science says. Your brain enters REM several times a night and most dreaming happens then, but the sleeping brain is bad at saving new memories. People who wake briefly more often tend to remember more. #dreams #rememberdreams #dreamjournal #remsleep #sleepscience
Penguin sleep: one block or fragments? Studied nesting chinstrap penguins slept in bouts averaging about four seconds. Libourel et al. · 2023. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Some people punch their partner in their dreams. In REM sleep behaviour disorder the body acts out dreams. In a large study, 73.5% developed Parkinson's or a related disorder within 12 years (Postuma et al., 2019). #remsleep #sleepdisorder #parkinsons #sleepscience

Cavefish versus surface fish: more sleep or less? Three studied cave populations of Mexican tetra slept much less than surface fish of the same species. Duboué et al. · 2011. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

Millions have seen him at night. In sleep paralysis you wake up unable to move, and many people see or sense an intruder. About 7.6% of people have had it at least once (Sharpless & Barber, 2011). Have you? #sleepparalysis #shadowman #truestory #sleepscience

Dream about being chased meaning: what science says. In a survey of 1,181 students, being chased was the most common of 55 dream themes (81.5% at least once). One idea is threat rehearsal, still debated. #dreammeaning #beingchased #dreams #nightmares #sleepscience

Teeth falling out dream meaning: what science says. In one study of 210 students, teeth dreams weren't linked to distress or poor sleep, but went with tension in the teeth, gums or jaw on waking. Linked, not proven. #dreammeaning #teethfallingout #dreams #teethdream #sleepscience

People drove cars while fully asleep. In 2019 the FDA added a boxed warning to zolpidem, eszopiclone and zaleplon after 66 serious cases of sleepwalking, sleep driving and other complex sleep behaviours, 20 of them deaths. #truestory #sleepdriving #sleepwalking #sleepscience

Night terrors vs nightmares: what's the difference? Night terrors usually happen early in the night, in deep sleep, and are rarely remembered; nightmares come in dream sleep, later on, and usually are (NHS, AASM). #nightterrors #nightmares #sleep #parenting #sleepscience

There is a disease that ends sleep. Fatal familial insomnia is an inherited prion disease that takes away the ability to sleep. It is extremely rare, and ordinary insomnia does not turn into it. #sleepscience #insomnia #brain #didyouknow
#bodyfacts #didyouknow #sleep

Are you taller in the morning? Yes, by about 2 cm. In a 1984 study, height peaked on waking and was about 1.1% lower by midnight: spine discs lose volume when you are upright and refill when you lie down. It varies by person. #taller #bodyfacts #didyouknow #sleep #spine

She was found asleep on a crane. London, 2005: a sleepwalking 15-year-old climbed a crane and was found asleep about 40 m up. Firefighters brought her down unharmed. #truestory #sleepwalking #london #sleepscience

Does sleep need a central brain? Cassiopea jellyfish showed a sleep-like state without a centralized nervous system. Nath et al. · 2017. #sleep #sleepscience #nightmind #science

He killed while asleep. Then he was acquitted. Toronto, 1987: Ken Parks drove to his in-laws' house while sleepwalking. Canada's Supreme Court upheld his acquittal in 1992. Has anyone in your family sleepwalked? #truestory #sleepwalking #truecrime #sleepscience

How long should it take to fall asleep? About 10 to 20 minutes. Dropping off almost instantly, night after night, can be a sign of sleep debt. Fine if you wake refreshed; if you are tired every day, talk to a doctor. #fallasleep #sleeptips #sleepscience #sleep #tired

Why do I wake up at 3am? What sleep science says. Brief wake-ups are normal, 3 to 4 a.m. is a body-clock turning point, and a 2022 hypothesis says night tilts mood negative. If it keeps costing you sleep, talk to a doctor. #3am #cantsleep #insomnia #sleepscience #sleep

Do you swallow spiders in your sleep? Myth check. A spider expert at the Burke Museum (University of Washington) says no case is on formal record, and a sleeper's vibrations tend to warn spiders away. An expert's view, not a study. #spiders #sleepmyths #mythbusting #sleep #didyouknow

Your dreams rarely replay your day. In a 2003 study, 29 people kept a daily log and wrote down dreams for 14 days. About 65% of 299 dream reports were judged to reflect recent life, yet whole-episode replays appeared in no more than 1 to 2%. Pieces, not reruns. #dreams #sleepscience #psychology #brain #didyouknow
Teeth falling in your sleep 😴

Can a brain scan guess what you dream? In a 2013 Science study from Kyoto, a model trained on scans of people looking at pictures picked object categories in sleep-onset imagery from three volunteers, right about 60% of the time on average (chance 50%). Categories, not films. #dreams #sleepscience #neuroscience #brain #didyouknow

You can dream outside REM sleep too. In a 2017 sleep-lab study using high-density EEG, people woken from REM and from non-REM sleep reported dreams, and activity in a back-of-brain hot zone tracked whether they dreamed. One lab, so treat it as a strong clue, not the last word. #dreams #sleepscience #neuroscience #brain #didyouknow

Asleep, your nose is a poor alarm. Your ears aren't. In a small 2004 Brown University lab study (6 young adults), peppermint got no response in deeper sleep and harsh pyridine only some, while a tone got a response on at least 75% of trials. Smoke itself wasn't tested. #sleepscience #sleepfacts #brain #psychology #didyouknow

Falling asleep in under 5 minutes is not a flex. Normal sleep latency is around 10 to 20 minutes. Dropping off almost instantly, night after night, can be a sign of sleep debt rather than great sleep. If it's every night and you're tired by day, talk to a doctor. #sleepscience #fallingasleep #sleepdebt #brain #psychology

Why do your worries feel bigger after midnight? One sleep researcher says 3 to 4 a.m. is a body-clock turning point when we're at our lowest ebb and alone in the dark. A 2022 hypothesis says night tilts mood negative. Brief wake-ups are normal. #3amthoughts #sleepscience #psychology #overthinking #brain

Your brain stays on guard in a new bed. In a 35-person Brown University study, a network in the left half of the brain slept lighter on night one and woke people faster to odd sounds. By night two, the difference was gone. #sleepscience #firstnighteffect #travel #brain #fallingasleep

In mice, sleep widened the gaps between brain cells and waste cleared faster. Sleeping humans show big fluid waves. But a 2024 mouse study found the opposite, so the debate is open. #sleepscience #brain #neuroscience #glymphatic #3amthoughts

It's called exploding head syndrome: a scary name for a painless sleep-onset glitch. In one study, 18% of college students said it had happened to them at least once. #explodingheadsyndrome #sleepscience #fallingasleep #brain #psychology

It's hypnagogia: the drowsy border where images drift in. Over a third of people report it, and it may even be a creative sweet spot. #hypnagogia #sleepscience #fallingasleep #psychology #dreamy

This line was built in 1898 during the Gold Rush and it still runs today.
